0.long_answer: Alpha-1 antitrypsin is a serine protease inhibitor that plays a key role in regulating proteolytic enzymes which, when unchecked, can degrade elastin in the aortic wall. The gene encoding alpha-1 antitrypsin, SERPINA1, is located on chromosome 14. Deficiency in alpha-1 antitrypsin leads to an imbalance between proteases and their inhibitors, resulting in excessive breakdown of elastin. This degradation weakens the structural integrity of the aortic wall and may elevate the risk of developing an abdominal aortic aneurysm.
